hypotheses.title: Analyst Post-Earnings Sell-the-News Reversal (Rank Difference)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Empirical revision of SUE hypothesis: When actual EPS exceeds consensus mean, the announcement triggers immediate profit taking and expectations exhaustion. Inverting the sign captures this post-earnings reversal. Furthermore, using cross-sectional rank differences eliminates unit incompatibility between price-based actuals and consensus forecasts.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha fails if post-earnings drift continues in the direction of the surprise rather than reversing against subindustry peers.

candidates.rationale: Inverted rank-difference earnings surprise with 60-day quarterly backfill

hypotheses.title: Customer Return Momentum Overshoot & Supplier Mean Reversion
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Empirical revision of customer momentum spillover: 10-day customer positive return spikes cause immediate over-optimism and subsequent mean-reversion in supplier valuations. Inverting the signal captures this mean-reversion with consistent sub-universe Sharpe stability.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if supplier momentum persists in the direction of customer returns rather than mean-reverting.

candidates.rationale: Inverted cumulative customer return signal with 5-day backfill

hypotheses.title: Volatility Term Structure Persistence & Clustering
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Empirical revision of volatility term structure: When near-term 20-day historical volatility expands relative to the 180-day baseline, volatility clustering and institutional hedging demand persist. Removing the negative sign aligns the formula with momentum in volatility risk premium.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if high short-term volatility collapses immediately without price continuation.

candidates.rationale: Upward volatility ratio continuation with 20-day backfill
